scenarios.title: Check address claims before forwarding ARP
scenarios.summary: Use confirmed DHCP address records to admit valid ARP and reject unsupported address claims.
scenarios.objective: Inspect ARP on both user-facing paths in VLAN 10. Admit the DHCP workstation's valid claims and the approved server's replies, while rejecting another workstation claiming 10.30.0.10 or the DHCP workstation claiming a different address. After the supplied lease expires, stop admitting that old DHCP claim.
steps: Investigate the supplied address claims, repair the policy and verify both admitted and rejected traffic.
scenarios.explanation: Inspect VLAN 10 and keep client and peer untrusted for ARP. Allow the approved server path with its separate ARP trust setting or a suitable exact address-list rule. Replay valid and false claims and the expired record; keep both user paths inspected.
hints: DHCP trust was already supplied; this separate policy controls incoming ARP.
The valid claim is checked and delivered; a forged or expired claim is rejected.
The exemption admits unwanted traffic. Checking every case detects it even if the valid exchange still works.
scenarios.simplifications: Checked2026-11-08: CCNA200-301v1.1/5.7; RFC826 and Catalyst9300 IOS XE Dublin17.12 DAI chapter2023-07-28, supporting Cisco2222742024-08-05. One supplied access LAN; typed Request/Reply metadata and real virtual recipients, not packet bytes, a host ARP cache, ping, IOS, authentication or equipment conformance. DHCP setup is supplied and read-only here. Address-list rules match exact IP/MAC pairs; wildcard lists, trunks/stacks, full rate/log/counter scheduling and IPSG are excluded. A matching DHCP pair on a different port is explicitly unsupported rather than assigned guessed behavior. The simulator permits at most8 ARP arrivals per virtual second, below the hardware rate; exceeding that guard produces a simulator-limit diagnostic, not a fabricated device drop/error-disable. Case replays start separate sample networks; checks leave displayed observations unchanged. A zero sender IP on inspected untrusted ingress is unsupported with the optional IP check off; probe-specific handling is not guessed.

After the supplied lease expires, stop admitting that old DHCP claim.

example.instructions: In the sample LAN, enable ARP inspection for VLAN 10 and allow the approved server's incoming ARP. Replay a valid workstation claim, a forged claim and expiry; compare actual recipients and DHCP records.

scenarios.title: Keep a static workstation working without trusting its port
scenarios.summary: Repair an exact IP/MAC address-list entry and its interaction with DHCP records.
scenarios.objective: Permit the static workstation at 10.30.0.99 with the MAC shown in the topology, while inspecting its ARP instead of trusting its entire port. Reject the supplied unexpected static identity and its claims to another address. Keep the DHCP workstation's current claims working and reject them after its recorded lease expires.
steps: Investigate the supplied address claims, repair the policy and verify both admitted and rejected traffic.
scenarios.explanation: Correct the static workstation’s address-list MAC to the topology value, permit its supplied IP/MAC pair, and retain DHCP fallback by clearing the static-only option. Keep the static port inspected. Do not permanently permit the DHCP client, because that would ignore lease expiry.
hints: The list admits the static sender; other DHCP senders can fall back to their current records.
Correct static and DHCP claims pass inspection. The supplied different static MAC must be rejected.
A permanent list rule survives lease expiry. Falling back to DHCP records preserves the expiry boundary.

scenarios.title: Diagnose inconsistent Ethernet and ARP fields
scenarios.summary: Compare packet headers with their ARP contents without blocking ordinary requests.
scenarios.objective: Reject the supplied requests and replies whose Ethernet source differs from the ARP sender MAC, and the reply whose destination differs from its ARP target MAC. Keep valid requests and replies working, including a request with an unknown target MAC. Continue rejecting an unknown sender's address claim.
steps: Investigate the supplied address claims, repair the policy and verify both admitted and rejected traffic.
scenarios.explanation: Enable source-MAC comparison and reply destination/target-MAC comparison on inspected ingress. Keep the client port inspected and verify legitimate requests with an unknown target MAC and valid replies. Do not replace these checks with trust.
hints: Source and reply-target discrepancies are different checks. The actual fields remain visible beside Replay.
They are now rejected for the specific disagreement.
The ordinary cases still pass; removing a comparison fails only the relevant mismatch cases rather than every case.
